Title: Limited research
Description: Just a simple research. Web searching, AI asking and putting it all together in a dataset.

Title: Customer focus research
Description: Who is your main customer? Who will benefit from your service? How can you deliver a value?

Title: Technical focus research
Description: How to make what you wana make? What technologies would you use? How can they work together?

Title: Full scale research
Description: You throw all your resources and efforts to make your product the best fit possible. It will help in a long run... probably.

Title: Essential prototype
Description: This prototipe will just show that your idea works. It is ugly. It is buggy. But it proves the very basic concept.

Title: Service prototype
Description: This isn't a technical prototype. You have your landing page up and running, and you should do everything else by hand with every client.

Title: Technical prototype
Description: Now you know, that everything is working on the technical side. User experience? Never heard about this.

Title: Product MVP
Description: This MVP proves everything and you can ship it to selected audience. It is well designed. Well built. And it took time and effort to make it this early.

Title: Mission only
Description: Now your crew knows why are you doing what you are doing.

Title: Values and Strategy
Description: Values will help your team to make important decisions. Strategy will navigate them on which decisions they should make.

Title: Values and Mission
Description: Values will help your team to make important decisions. Mission will give them purpose to make these decisions.

Title: Values, Mission and Strategy
Description: You have done it all. Now your team knows why, how, and which decisions they should make. It invokes confidence.

Title: Internal testing
Description: Your team and friends are enough to test your product. There is no need to gather the audience.

Title: Medium focus group testing
Description: Your testing group consists of a few dozens of people both from your audience and new ones. It will help to catch criticals in your product.

Title: Real-world testing
Description: It is relatively good idea to just put your product online and acquire some users to simply use it. If you are ready to rapidly fix all appearing problems.

Title: Cascade testing with user groups
Description: Full-scale testing with several stages, each bigger. You have prepared and made it all

Title: Website building
Description: You definitely need a website. Anything else? Probaply, not.

Title: Social media setup
Description: Who needs a website when you can make it all with a proper social media account?

Title: Website and Social Media
Description: It is often easier to gather audience via social media, but they should be landed somewhere.

Title: Full marketing commitment
Description: Social media, website, community hub, press releases, and contacts with influencers. You should have it all to succeed.

Title: Single server
Description: Simple backand will be more then enough. So why bother and spend additional money on an ifrastructure? What could possibly go wrong?

Title: Cloud infrastructure
Description: Why should we bother to make our own server if we can use a cloud? It is a little bit more expensive, but definitely much more convenient.

Title: Multiple servers
Description: We know how to make it on our own with all the redundancy we need to provide a consistent service to our clients.

Title: DevOPS team with an infrastructure
Description: Infrastructure needs to be carfully planned and maintained. So we need to hire a DevOPS team to help use make this project.

Title: Self application
Description: Just prepare all the documents and send it according to instructions on a DPG website.

Title: Contact DPG office to assist
Description: We can make it with the DPG office, if they are able to help.

Title: Address SDG relevance only
Description: You have checked if your product is SDG relevant or not. If it is - so why bother? It will work anyway.

Title: DPG indicator checklist
Description: You have your checklist, so you go thugh all 9 indicators and prepare properly your application.

Title: Release marketing campaign
Description: Your team is fully focused on a marketing campaign for the release. The technical side of things is not in focus.

Title: Release event
Description: Just throw a release event to attract an audience. They will watch the stream and then they will use your product.

Title: Some release preparations
Description: You clearly have not enough time to make it all, but you can address the majore issues and prepare the campaign on a decent level.

Title: Full scale release preparations
Description: Your team is working on the release, giving attention to everything. It will take time. But since you have one, you can afford it.

Title: Essential support only
Description: We don't have enough resources for the full scale support, so we will do only bare essentials.

Title: Phone and email customer support
Description: We will conduct a customer support via both phone and email.

Title: Support with LiveOPS
Description: We will not only make a support up and running, but also establish regular events and activities for our clients (LiveOPS).

Title: Outsourced support
Description: We no need our team to make a customer support. Let's hire an outsource company to make it for us!

Title: Desk research
Description: Read forestry reports, satellite studies and news about the dry Aral seabed. Cheap and fast, but you only see the problem from a distance.

Title: Ride with foresters
Description: Spend a few weeks with the forestry crews of Aralsk and Kazaly. Learn how they plant saxaul, what they write down on paper and what gets lost.

Title: Satellite data survey
Description: Find out which free satellite images can show young saxaul from space, how sharp they are and how often they update.

Title: Full field expedition
Description: A long expedition across the seabed: interviews in villages, soil samples, test photos and a visit to every kind of planting site.

Title: Paper prototype
Description: Sketch the screens on paper and walk the foresters through them over tea. Quick feedback, no code.

Title: Offline form prototype
Description: A simple mobile form that saves a planting with GPS and a photo even with no signal, and syncs when the phone is back in range.

Title: Satellite overlay demo
Description: Put planting points on top of satellite images to check whether green patches on the map match what crews report.

Title: Clickable field app
Description: A working prototype with offline forms, a planting map and a survival checklist, tested by two real forestry crews.

Title: Hire a local intern
Description: A student from the Kyzylorda college joins you. Knows the roads, the villages and speaks with the crews in their own language.

Title: Hire a GIS developer
Description: Someone who really understands maps, coordinates and satellite layers. Hard to find, but it shows in the code.

Title: Hire a field coordinator
Description: A person who lives near the seabed, organises crews and volunteers and makes sure the app is actually used in the field.

Title: Build a full team
Description: Take your time and hire a balanced team: developer, GIS specialist, field coordinator and a designer.

Title: Planting log only
Description: The smallest useful product: crews log where, when and how many saxaul seedlings they planted. Nothing else.

Title: Log and survival checks
Description: Crews can return to a planting a year later and mark each plot as alive, dried out or buried by sand.

Title: Log and public map
Description: Every planting appears on an open public map, so villagers and donors can see where work is being done.

Title: Full MVP
Description: Planting log, survival checks, public map and photo history in one release. Impressive, but the team is exhausted.

Title: Survey foresters
Description: Send a short questionnaire to every forestry office in the region and ask what they would really use.

Title: Pilot in one district
Description: One district forestry office uses the app for a full planting season. Real data, real problems.

Title: Volunteer planting day
Description: Invite students and families to plant saxaul for a day and log every seedling in the app.

Title: Three district pilot
Description: Three districts, dozens of crews and thousands of seedlings. Expensive, but it proves the idea at scale.

Title: Fix pilot bugs
Description: Go through every complaint from the pilot and fix what annoyed the crews the most.

Title: Kazakh and Russian UI
Description: Translate the whole app and its help texts so that every crew member can use it in the language they prefer.

Title: Automatic satellite check
Description: The app compares each planting with fresh satellite images and flags plots that seem to have died.

Title: Open data export
Description: Anyone can download the planting and survival data in common open formats for their own research.

Title: Choose open licenses
Description: Pick an open source license for the code and an open license for the planting data, and state it clearly.

Title: Do no harm review
Description: Check that the map never exposes private homes, herders' winter camps or personal data of volunteers, and document it.

Title: Documentation sprint
Description: Write setup guides, a data dictionary and a contributor guide so others can run and improve the project.

Title: Full DPG package
Description: Licenses, privacy review, documentation, SDG evidence and ownership papers, all prepared at once.

Title: Quiet release
Description: Publish the app and the code without any noise. The crews already know about it.

Title: Launch at an Aral forum
Description: Present the app at a regional conference on the Aral Sea in front of scientists, officials and donors.

Title: Train every crew
Description: Travel to each forestry office and run a hands on training before the release.

Title: Region wide campaign
Description: Radio, posters in every village and school lessons about saxaul. Everyone in the region will hear about the app.

Title: Community moderators
Description: Trusted volunteers check new records, fix obvious mistakes and answer questions from new users.

Title: Hand over to forestry
Description: The regional forestry department takes over daily use, while your team keeps maintaining the code.

Title: Own support team
Description: Build your own support team that helps crews every day and runs survival checks each season.

Title: Seasonal monitoring cycle
Description: Set up a yearly rhythm: plant in spring, check survival in autumn, publish an open report every winter.
